metadata_contract.purpose: Exact existing direct principal/current DB/RR READ ONLY/connect5s/statement5s/lock5s/transaction15s/current snapshot before and after; fail on elevation, wrong identity or unexpected parent memberships before target metadata.

Exactly two fixed qualified names -> existence/OID/namespaceOID/ownerOID+role name/kind/row-security flags/view security options; reject missing, duplicate, unsupported relation kind or identity change. Missing object is not a privilege denial.

Complete ordered attnum>0 metadata for BOTH targets, distinguish dropped attributes from live visible columns. Freeze actual names/typeOID/typmod/collation/attnum/not-null and raw-ACL NULL-versus-explicit state. No column values/default expressions/attmissingval/source data. Must include every currently visible view column because frozen original batch SQL uses SELECT *. Reject incomplete/duplicate ordering or incomplete evidence; never equate 44 static served fields with all live columns.

Full raw and normalized table/view/schema and column ACL metadata for only the two targets and mf namespace, including grantor/grantee/options. Preserve NULL/raw ACL state; derive default ACL via documented acldefault for NULL only, not current pg_default_acl. Do not confuse owner implicit capability with an explicit grant or claim current defaults govern existing objects.

Under exact reader: schema USAGE/CREATE, table-level SELECT and write/grant options, and EACH live column SELECT/write/grant options for two targets. Table-level SELECT may be false under a future approved column profile; has_any_column_privilege alone is never a complete column proof. No grant statements. Additionally, for EVERY relation/column reference in the complete declared dependency graph, record metadata-only effective SELECT under its derived actual access-check principal; preserve referenced-column sub-IDs/whole-row references and exact applicable column population. This is metadata privilege inquiry, never selecting data or granting underlying privileges.

Snapshot metadata for role-membership paths connected to the reader in BOTH directions, preserving grantor/admin/inherit/set options. Parent memberships/elevation drift fails the dedicated direct-reader gate. Child/grantee membership exposure must remain visible even when reader's own parent membership count is zero. Do not query password-bearing pg_authid or role settings.

Retrieve complete fixed view definition into private worker memory, hash exact bytes and suppress raw SQL body in logs/certificate. Retain complete metadata dependency edges for its SELECT rewrite and recursively referenced views through pg_rewrite+pg_depend, including referenced column sub-IDs, object classes/OIDs/kinds/owners/security modes/definition hashes. Full closure through catalog-declared relation/rewrite dependencies; never truncate or claim completeness after timeout/transport failure. Unexpected dependency class/kind, cycle handling ambiguity or unavailable metadata fails or explicitly blocks access-plan admission. Derive and retain the root requesting principal and effective access-check principal at EVERY nested view boundary from actual security_invoker options and view ownership. Default owner-checked and invoker-checked edges must be distinct; do not assume all relations are checked as the root reader or as one global owner.

For function/operator references in that declared closure: metadata signatures/OIDs/owner/security-definer/volatility/leakproof flags and effective EXECUTE booleans for reader and relevant view owner, including operator->function mapping. Never execute a target function, read prosrc/probin/credential text or assume catalog dependencies describe dynamic procedural SQL/calls. Any unmodeled/dynamic/unknown dependency remains an explicit unresolved owner-review blocker; no claim of full runtime safety.

For each target and every relation reached by the complete declared dependency closure, bind the actual access-check principal derived at each nested-view boundary, its relevant role memberships, superuser/BYPASSRLS flags, relation ownership, row_security/FORCE RLS flags and applicable policies (command/role memberships/permissiveness/qual-with-check hashes). Distinguish normal owner bypass, FORCE RLS, superuser/BYPASSRLS and invoker security contexts according to PostgreSQL18. Catalogue flags/policy hashes are NOT a proof of rows returned or policy-expression/function safety. Unknown/ambiguous principal propagation, missing column SELECT, unknown policy applicability, unsupported/dynamic dependency or incomplete metadata MUST block access-profile admission. No data/view/RLS/function execution or underlying grants.

One RR READ ONLY transaction, hash full metadata at entry and end according to fixed query inventory. Same transaction/snapshot equality proves only consistent captured metadata, not absence of concurrent changes outside its snapshot. Any future grant needs a newly approved fresh before fingerprint and race guard; never reuse this snapshot as writer permission.

consumer_and_grantor_limits.known_consumers: At delivery readiness, inspect only the existing approved fixed protected service/job profiles and their pinned secret references. No namespace-wide executions list, pg_stat_activity/pg_stat_statements, arbitrary secret reads, auth-token printing or unknown provider calls.
consumer_and_grantor_limits.not_complete_consumer_inventory: Role-membership edges and known protected references do NOT discover every session/client or all copies of a DSN. Owner must separately attest allowed consumers; unknown consumers remain a blocker before shared-role grant.
consumer_and_grantor_limits.grantor: Metadata may identify owners and existing ACL grantors. That does not prove an operating grantor credential is available/authorized; no admin secret access, role switch, owner fallback or IAM bootstrap.
consumer_and_grantor_limits.dependency_principals: Role/membership metadata may expand only to actual owner/invoker/policy principals referenced by the fixed two-root dependency graph, never a blanket all-role or all-database scan. Complete graph and explicit unresolved cases are mandatory; result transport/5s5s15s failure is terminal, not a reason to omit a branch.

Include nested default-owner/invoker combinations, different view owners, owner lacking a referenced column SELECT, direct and inherited policy-role applicability, owner versus FORCE RLS, superuser/BYPASSRLS and ambiguous/unmodelled branches. A captured graph with unresolved dependency security must not be admitted as a grant profile.
